facts.text: Wilmot got its name from the railroad surveyor who laid out the town, and the Bartholomew post office moved there on April 7, 1892.
After Arkansas joined the Union in 1836, pioneer families like the Wilhites, Eatmans, Whites, and Gaines settled west of Bayou Bartholomew, forming Wilmot's early community.
Wilmot's fertile alluvial soils supported cotton, corn, and cypress, with steamboats ferrying produce from Lake Enterprise and Bayou Bartholomew to distant markets.
Lake Enterprise borders Wilmot, offering locals a popular spot for fishing and watersports amid the surrounding delta wetlands.
Today, Wilmot's economy centers on farming, forestry, fishing, and hunting, employing about 101 people and reflecting a median household income of $27,500.
